task4_limitation_language: The original one-shot Phase39 TEST protocol was not completed as intended. Two pre-outcome technical failures occurred (v1.0, v1.1); neither produced a scientific TEST result and neither was outcome-dependent. A post-protocol technical-recovery execution (v1.2) then successfully evaluated the frozen RA-MedFiLM-BARR system on all 1,683 TEST samples using the canonical frozen inference implementation. That recovery produced descriptive final-system segmentation results only: it did not emit the preregistered C-gGLOBAL comparative quantities (global-reference Dice, paired/macro DeltaDice, or their confidence intervals). Consequently the frozen comparative primary endpoint and the associated per-domain harm decisions could not be evaluated, and no additional TEST inference was performed to reconstruct them. The TEST evidence is therefore descriptive, not confirmatory, and is labelled: POST_PROTOCOL_TECHNICAL_RECOVERY_TEST_RESULT_WITH_TWO_DISCLOSED_PREOUTCOME_TECHNICAL_FAILURES.

task6_manuscript_viability.reasoning: The central contribution — the RA-MedFiLM-BARR architecture and its preservation / module-contribution claims — rests on frozen Phase27 (VAL808 preservation), Phase30 (one-shot ROUTER_HOLDOUT non-inferiority, with disclosed protocol-deviation qualifier), Phase28 (ablation), Phase29 (three-seed reproducibility), Phase33 (failure analysis), Phase34 (efficiency), Phase35 (interpretability) and Phase36 (robustness) evidence. None of those central claims depends on the missing Phase39 comparative endpoint. The Phase39 TEST was intended as the final untouched confirmation; its absence means the manuscript may present TEST only descriptively (final-system Dice by domain + macro) and must disclose the missing comparative endpoint. The TEST-confirmed variants of claims A and D remain unavailable.
